message.subject: Oil looks cloudy
message.body:
Good morning,

I wonder if you could help me with a small query. The oil from the order that arrived on the 10th of September has gone rather cloudy. We had a very cold night on Wednesday and I keep the bottle in the cupboard beside the back door, which does get chilly.

It did not look like this when it arrived. Is that normal when the weather turns cold, or has something gone wrong with it? I have put it aside for now until I hear from you.

Kind regards,
Grace Papadopoulos

policy.label: Policy P11.1: Product questions
policy.text:
Storage. Keep products below 25°C, out of direct sunlight, in their original packaging with the lid closed tightly, and out of reach of children and pets. They do not need to go in the fridge unless the label says so. Do not leave them in a car. Some oils can thicken or look cloudy when cold.

If a product looks, smells or tastes different, has been left somewhere hot, or a spray or dropper is not working, ask the patient not to use it until a pharmacist has checked. A pharmacist contacts them within 1 business day and arranges a replacement if needed. Agents never say a product is safe, fine or OK to use. If the patient asks whether it is still safe or OK to use, that is a clinical question: it goes to the clinician queue with no drafted reply (see clinical questions).

Packaging. Orders arrive in plain outer packaging. The label shows the patient's name and address only; it does not name the product or say it is medicine.

Availability and substitutions. If a product is out of stock, a clinician or pharmacist decides on any alternative, and the patient is told before anything changes. A different bottle size or format also needs a clinician's approval. Agents never recommend, compare or promote products. Unused or damaged medicine can be taken to any pharmacy for safe disposal.

policy.label: Policy P8.1: Account access, security and carers
policy.text:
Password resets. A reset link lasts 30 minutes, and a new link cancels any older one. If an email does not arrive, check spam, then check the email address on the account. Five wrong passwords lock the account for 30 minutes.

Login codes. Two-step codes are sent by SMS to the phone number on the account, and can be turned on under Security in the account. If codes do not arrive, support can switch codes to email after an identity check.

Identity check. Before changing an email address, phone number, delivery address or payment details, confirm two of: date of birth, postcode on file, and most recent order number. Never ask for a password or a full card number.

Carers and representatives. A carer or family member can act for a patient once the patient has listed them on the account with consent. We always accept information from anyone about a patient's health or safety, or a report that a patient has died, and act on it, but we do not share details or change the account for someone who is not listed.

policy.label: Policy P2.2: Talking to a person and complaints
policy.text:
A patient can always talk to a person. Offer a call back at a time they choose, within 1 business day, or live chat during support hours. When a patient asks for a person, a team member writes the reply; there is no automated reply. Never make a patient ask twice, and never send them back to a help article instead.

Complaints: acknowledge within 1 business day, give the patient the name of the person who owns the complaint, and aim to resolve it within 10 business days. The team lead reviews every complaint. Complaints about clinical care go to the clinical lead, and complaints about privacy go to the privacy officer. If we cannot resolve a complaint, tell the patient how to contact the independent health complaints body in their country.
